about: Candidate playbook for Blood Rites (Clavileno, First of the Blessed), written from 12 stock goldfish games on seeds 26001-26012.

playbook.notes: Clavileno makes an attacking Vampire a Demon that draws a card and leaves a 4/3 flier when it dies, so the deck is Vampires that attack every turn with drain and lifegain on top. Stock Forge plays it fairly well in goldfish (12.4 turns, 12 of 12 kills) and leaves 43% of its mana unspent, but most of that is answers it rightly holds against do-nothing opponents. What it does leave undone: the commander late behind rocks it has (Sol Ring and Talisman out, Clavileno on turn 5 and Elenda held for four turns in game 7), anthems and engine permanents held (Kindred Boon, Glass-Cast Heart, Elenda's Hierophant held for many turns), Viscera Seer never cast (flagged), March of the Canonized barely cast. The rules: rocks, then the commander, then the anthems and engine permanents in order of worth, Champion of Dusk only with three Vampires and a library and life to pay for it, then the bodies; March of the Canonized for all the mana at X 3 or more; Viscera Seer is cast as a 1-mana Vampire but its scry outlet stays shut (Forge would feed it creatures); Glass-Cast Heart makes a lifelink Vampire with mana left after combat. Trigger rules take Bloodghast, Heirloom Blade, Bloodline Necromancer and Timothar always and Crossway Troublemakers' card while life and library allow. Answers (Swords, Utter End, Return to Dust, New Blood, Damn, Austere Command, Olivia's Wrath, Patron of the Vein, Butcher of Malakir's sacrifice, Vona's ability) are left to Forge in this pass. Go-wide attack, highest life first. Rule 9 equips Blade of the Bloodchief and Heirloom Blade before combat where Forge's own logic agrees on a carrier (it declined most offers in tuning); the last trigger rule takes Promise of Aclazotz's end-step populate once there is a token to copy and four creatures. Tuning on the audit seeds: 0.9 turns faster than stock (12 seeds), the last two additions neutral.
